hypothesis: The four coarse pitch groups hide control-relevant repertoire differences within fastballs and breaking balls. Historical fine pitch labels can define pitcher-by-fine-type control residuals, while a classifier using only legal pre-pitch row fields can marginalize those residuals without observing the current pitch type at inference.

relationship_to_prior_work.v5_pitchtype_moe: used only four coarse groups and four subset-trained outcome experts
relationship_to_prior_work.v4_pitchtype_failure_prior: used empirical contextual pitch counts around a V4 research ensemble; this experiment uses an out-of-time CatBoost fine-type selector, exact-C source anchors, and the V5 source gate
relationship_to_prior_work.current_pitch_trackman: true fine type is diagnostic-only and can never enter a deployable prediction

source_protocol.history: season strictly less than source year
source_protocol.route: R rows only; F predictions remain exact-C

selector.features: official pre-pitch base columns including historical IDs and asof rates

control_prior.target: control_success minus its matched R season mean
control_prior.cells: pitcher_id by historical fine pitch type
control_prior.correction: expected contextual fine-type residual minus frozen historical repertoire expectation

selection_rule: maximize the minimum exact-C full-score gain across 2020 and 2021, then minimum R gain, with all probability weights and correction scales fixed from this source screen
next_step_if_pass: preregister a shared fine-type conditional model before reading 2022 labels
next_step_if_fail: close the fine-pitch latent axis without opening 2022 or later labels
